svg.title: Random Forest, Part 1 — From One Big Tree to a Voting Forest
svg.text: Random Forest, Part 1 — From One Big Tree to a Voting Forest
1. Train one big decision tree on all 1000 rows.
✗ One big tree is not good: it memorises the 1000 training rows (overfits) and changes a lot when the data changes.
2. Bootstrap: draw 1000 rows from the dataset with replacement → a new sample → grow a small tree. Repeat.
Each sample is a little different,
so each small tree is a little different.
3. Keep going: tree 4, tree 5, tree 6 … until there are 100 small trees. That is the forest.
4. A new input row goes to every tree. Each tree votes; the majority decides.
one big decision tree (depth 4, 15 nodes … in practice much deeper)
